title: The day before the Constitution was adopted, its own architect warned the country not to trust it blindly.

sources.text: Supreme Court of India - Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's Closing Speech, 25 Nov 1949

caption:
The day before the Constitution was adopted, its own architect warned the country not to trust it blindly.

In the speech, Ambedkar warned that a good constitution alone couldn't guarantee good governance - if things went wrong, he said, it wouldn't be because the Constitution was bad, but because the people entrusted to run it failed to live up to it.

Ambedkar's closing argument was that a constitution is only as good as the people who operate it - a caution aimed at every future generation, not just the one adopting it the next day.

Nearly 80 years later, that warning is still the standard the country is measured against, not just the text of the Constitution itself.
